fixtures.transcript: We need a controlled release investigation for the dictation pipeline, and the result has to be useful rather than flattering. Begin with the same recorded audio for every speech engine so that microphone timing, room noise, pauses, and pronunciation do not move between runs. Store the reference transcript beside the audio, then calculate ordinary word error rate and a separate technical-term recall score. The technical list should include NATA, Gitter repositories, ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, SwiftPM, MLX, FluidAudio, Qwen, Nemotron, bundle identifiers, file paths, command flags, URLs, email addresses, versions, percentages, and units. Do not let a good score on common prose hide failures on the words that matter during development. For post-processing, feed every candidate the same raw transcript rather than allowing each speech engine to produce a different input. Record cold model load, warm prompt prefill, first generated token, final generated token, edit validation, text reconstruction, and destination insertion as separate timings. A full rewrite that takes 10 seconds and then types for another 2.5 seconds is not competitive just because model loading happened earlier. A structured edit run must still be rejected if it changes /Users/ian/dev/native/natter, drops release 0.1.0, alters 5.24%, changes 560 ms, removes ian@example.com, or rewrites https://example.com/releases. Run enough iterations to report p50 and p95 without treating the first warm result as the whole story. Medium transcripts should cover roughly 150 to 350 words. Long transcripts should cover roughly 350 to 800 words. Stress transcripts should go beyond that and must prove the raw source remains recoverable even when a model reaches its context or output limit. On this machine, the initial acceptance target is warm Agent post-processing below 2 seconds at p50 for about 350 words and below 3 seconds at p50 for about 700 words. The p95 targets are below 3 seconds and below 5 seconds respectively. Natter must also beat the comparable Monologue local result by at least 25 percent in each representative bucket. Compare end-to-end stop-to-finished latency separately from model-only latency because terminal pacing and inaccessible text controls are delivery problems, not inference problems. Keep Email and Article on the full Qwen rewrite path because those modes intentionally restructure prose. Agent should use the compact edit path because most technical dictation needs only a few corrected identifiers, punctuation marks, or explicit spoken forms. Set scroll restoration: true only when that exact property is requested. Keep the main actor annotation where the coordinator owns user-interface state, and inspect app delegate before moving launch code. The validator must require every edit source to be an exact, case-sensitive, unique substring. It must reject overlapping ranges, more than sixteen edits, absent source text, ambiguous repeated source text, and a total change budget above one third of the transcript, while ignoring an unchanged replacement. Apply accepted ranges from the end toward the beginning so earlier string indices remain valid. After reconstruction, run the protected-fact guard over the complete output. If any check fails, preserve the original raw record and deliver the safe deterministic transcript rather than cascading into another generative rewrite. The model prompt can include a bounded local glossary. Preferred spellings should come from the user's dictionary, the destination application, the current project, and a small built-in set for Natter's own stack. User-defined spellings are authoritative. Built-in hints are contextual and must never become a giant global replacement table. A phrase such as Gitter chat can remain unchanged, while Gitter repository is strong evidence for GitHub. The term NATA can remain an organisation in ordinary prose, while using NATA to describe this dictation app is strong evidence for Natter. Keep this context local and do not introduce telemetry, accounts, cloud inference, Ollama, a Homebrew helper, or a localhost service. Once the model benchmark passes, rebuild the signed application through xcodebuild so the MLX Metal shader bundle sits beside the executable. Then test ordinary native fields, Safari, Chrome, Gmail, ChatGPT Desktop, Claude Desktop, Terminal, iTerm, and Ghostty. Include focus changes, screenshots pasted during a recording, Raw delivery, buffered Agent delivery, cancellation, Paste Last Transcript, and recovery after the original text field disappears. Report failures honestly, keep the exact transcript available, and do not call the performance goal complete until every named latency and safety gate has direct evidence.
